18	How rule registration works
19	---------------------------
20	- Rule metadata lives in ``utils/check_modeling_structure_rules.toml``.
21	- Executable TRF rules are auto-discovered from functions named ``trfXXX_*``.
22	- The ``trfXXX`` prefix becomes the rule id (for example ``trf003_check_...`` -> ``TRF003``).
23	- Every discovered rule must have a matching entry in the TOML file, and every TOML rule must have a matching
24	  ``trfXXX_*`` function. Import-time validation fails if either side is missing.
25	- Rule functions receive ``rule_id`` explicitly and should use it for suppression checks and violation messages.
26	- Suppressions use ``# trf-ignore: TRFXXX`` on the same line or the line immediately above the flagged construct.
27	
28	How to add a new TRF rule
29	-------------------------
30	1. Add a ``[rules.TRFXXX]`` entry to ``utils/check_modeling_structure_rules.toml``.
31	2. Fill in ``description``, ``default_enabled``, ``explanation.what_it_does``, ``explanation.why_bad``,
32	   ``explanation.bad_example``, and ``explanation.good_example``. Optional model-level exceptions go in
33	   ``allowlist_models``.
34	3. Implement a new function named ``trfXXX_<descriptive_name>`` with signature
35	   ``(tree, file_path, source_lines, violations, rule_id) -> list[Violation]``.
36	4. Use ``rule_id`` instead of hardcoding ``"TRFXXX"`` inside the check.
37	5. Add or update focused tests in ``tests/repo_utils/test_check_modeling_structure.py``.
38	
39	CLI usage
40	---------
41	- ``python utils/check_modeling_structure.py``: check all modeling, modular, and configuration files.
42	- ``python utils/check_modeling_structure.py --changed-only --base-ref origin/main``: only check files changed
43	  against a git base ref, plus local staged, unstaged, and untracked model source files.
44	- ``python utils/check_modeling_structure.py --list-rules``: print all available TRF rules and their default state.
45	- ``python utils/check_modeling_structure.py --rule TRF001``: show the detailed documentation for one rule from the
46	  TOML file.
47	- ``python utils/check_modeling_structure.py --enable-rules TRF003``: enable additional rules on top of the defaults.
48	- ``python utils/check_modeling_structure.py --enable-all-trf-rules``: enable every TRF rule, including ones disabled

50	- ``python utils/check_modeling_structure.py --github-annotations``: emit GitHub Actions error annotations.

"""
Lint modeling, modular, and configuration files under ``src/transformers/models`` for structural conventions.

How rule registration works
---------------------------
- Rule metadata lives in ``utils/mlinter/check_modeling_structure_rules.toml``.
- Executable TRF rules are auto-discovered from functions named ``trfXXX_*``.
- The ``trfXXX`` prefix becomes the rule id (for example ``trf003_check_...`` -> ``TRF003``).
- Every discovered rule must have a matching entry in the TOML file, and every TOML rule must have a matching
  ``trfXXX_*`` function. Import-time validation fails if either side is missing.
- Rule functions receive ``rule_id`` explicitly and should use it for suppression checks and violation messages.
- Suppressions use ``# trf-ignore: TRFXXX`` on the same line or the line immediately above the flagged construct.
- Larger rules can live in their own submodule (see :mod:`trf011`); the check function just needs to be importable
  into this module's namespace under its ``trfXXX_*`` name so auto-discovery can find it.

How to add a new TRF rule
-------------------------
1. Add a ``[rules.TRFXXX]`` entry to ``utils/mlinter/check_modeling_structure_rules.toml``.
2. Fill in ``description``, ``default_enabled``, ``explanation.what_it_does``, ``explanation.why_bad``,
   ``explanation.bad_example``, and ``explanation.good_example``. Optional model-level exceptions go in
   ``allowlist_models``.
3. Implement a new function named ``trfXXX_<descriptive_name>`` with signature
   ``(tree, file_path, source_lines, violations, rule_id) -> list[Violation]``.
4. Use ``rule_id`` instead of hardcoding ``"TRFXXX"`` inside the check.
5. Add or update focused tests in ``tests/repo_utils/test_mlinter.py``.

CLI usage
---------
- ``python utils/mlinter/mlinter.py``: check all modeling, modular, and configuration files.
- ``python utils/mlinter/mlinter.py --changed-only --base-ref origin/main``: only check files changed
  against a git base ref, plus local staged, unstaged, and untracked model source files.
- ``python utils/mlinter/mlinter.py --list-rules``: print all available TRF rules and their default state.
- ``python utils/mlinter/mlinter.py --rule TRF001``: show the detailed documentation for one rule from the
  TOML file.
- ``python utils/mlinter/mlinter.py --enable-rules TRF003``: enable additional rules on top of the defaults.
- ``python utils/mlinter/mlinter.py --enable-all-trf-rules``: enable every TRF rule, including ones disabled
  by default.
- ``python utils/mlinter/mlinter.py --github-annotations``: emit GitHub Actions error annotations.
"""

def _is_repo_utils_test(path: str) -> bool:
    """Return `True` when `path` points to a test under `tests/repo_utils`."""
